concepts.name: Gross domestic product definition
concepts.summary: State that GDP is the market value of final goods and services produced within a country in a period and recognise what it counts and excludes.

concepts.name: Real versus nominal values
concepts.summary: Explain why nominal values must be adjusted for price changes to show real changes in output or income.

concepts.name: Inflation and price indices
concepts.summary: Describe inflation as a sustained rise in the general price level and how a basket-based index measures it.

concepts.name: Unemployment rate measurement
concepts.summary: Explain how the unemployment rate is computed from the labour force and why people outside the labour force are not counted.

concepts.name: Economic growth and recessions
concepts.summary: Distinguish long-run growth from short-run fluctuations and recognise expansions, peaks, recessions and troughs.

concepts.name: Central bank and interest rates
concepts.summary: Recall that a central bank sets a policy interest rate that influences borrowing costs across the economy.

concepts.name: Government budget, deficit and debt
concepts.summary: Distinguish a deficit (an annual flow) from debt (an accumulated stock) and identify main taxes and spending.

misconceptions.text: A government deficit and the national debt are the same thing.
A rise in nominal GDP always means the economy produced more.
Falling inflation means prices are falling.

concepts.name: Expenditure approach to GDP
concepts.summary: Compute GDP from consumption, investment, government purchases and net exports and classify transactions into those components.

concepts.name: Types of unemployment
concepts.summary: Classify cases of unemployment as frictional, structural or cyclical and relate them to the natural rate.

concepts.name: Causes of inflation
concepts.summary: Apply demand-pull and cost-push explanations to scenarios and distinguish them.

concepts.name: Aggregate demand and supply
concepts.summary: Use the AD-AS diagram to show how demand and supply shifts change output and the price level.

concepts.name: Fiscal policy tools
concepts.summary: Predict the direction of effect on aggregate demand from changes in taxes and government spending.

concepts.name: Monetary policy tools
concepts.summary: Trace how interest rate changes and open market operations affect borrowing, spending and output.

concepts.name: Exchange rates and trade balance
concepts.summary: Explain how currency appreciation or depreciation affects exports, imports and the trade balance.

misconceptions.text: Zero unemployment is the goal of a healthy economy.
Buying stocks or used goods counts as investment in GDP.
A trade deficit always signals a weak economy.

concepts.name: Fiscal multiplier
concepts.summary: Calculate and interpret the multiplier from the marginal propensity to consume and note why real multipliers vary.

concepts.name: Short-run Phillips curve
concepts.summary: Analyse the inverse inflation-unemployment relation and why it shifts with expectations and supply shocks.

concepts.name: Money market and loanable funds
concepts.summary: Analyse how money supply, money demand and saving-investment balance determine interest rates.

concepts.name: Crowding out
concepts.summary: Analyse how government borrowing can raise interest rates and reduce private investment.

concepts.name: Long-run growth determinants
concepts.summary: Decompose growth into capital, labour and productivity contributions and explain diminishing returns to capital.

concepts.name: Balance of payments accounts
concepts.summary: Interpret current and financial account entries and why they offset each other.

concepts.name: Automatic stabilisers and lags
concepts.summary: Analyse how built-in stabilisers work and how recognition, decision and impact lags limit discretionary policy.

misconceptions.text: Policymakers can permanently lower unemployment by accepting higher inflation.
Government spending always raises GDP by the full multiplier amount.
Printing money is how central banks normally change interest rates.

concepts.name: Expectations and long-run neutrality
concepts.summary: Analyse how expectations make the long-run Phillips curve vertical and money neutral in the long run.

concepts.name: Monetary policy rules
concepts.summary: Evaluate rule-based versus discretionary policy and judge inflation targeting against alternatives.

concepts.name: Open-economy policy effects
concepts.summary: Evaluate how fiscal and monetary policy work under floating and fixed exchange rates with capital mobility.

concepts.name: Debt sustainability
concepts.summary: Assess whether a debt ratio is sustainable using interest rate, growth and primary balance.

concepts.name: Supply shocks and stagflation
concepts.summary: Analyse why supply shocks raise prices while lowering output and constrain policy responses.

concepts.name: Financial crises and balance sheets
concepts.summary: Analyse how leverage and asset price falls propagate into recessions.

concepts.name: Zero lower bound and unconventional policy
concepts.summary: Evaluate tools used when policy rates cannot fall further and their limits.

misconceptions.text: A government's debt is like a household's and must eventually be fully repaid.
Central banks can fix any recession by cutting rates.
Fiscal stimulus works the same way under every exchange rate regime.

concepts.name: DSGE and model assumptions
concepts.summary: Critique the assumptions, strengths and failures of microfounded macro models for policy analysis.

concepts.name: Empirical identification of shocks
concepts.summary: Evaluate methods for isolating causal effects of policy and shocks and their limits.

concepts.name: Time inconsistency and credibility
concepts.summary: Evaluate how incentives to deviate from announced plans undermine policy and why behaviour shifts with regimes.

concepts.name: Policy regime design
concepts.summary: Design monetary and fiscal frameworks that balance credibility, flexibility and accountability.

concepts.name: Crisis response synthesis
concepts.summary: Construct a coherent combination of monetary, fiscal and financial measures for a given crisis.

concepts.name: Global imbalances and currency unions
concepts.summary: Evaluate the costs and benefits of currency unions and persistent external imbalances.

concepts.name: Long-run secular trends
concepts.summary: Assess evidence on falling natural interest rates, productivity and demographics shaping policy room.

misconceptions.text: A well-fitted macro model can be used unchanged to predict the effects of a new policy regime.
Central bank independence guarantees low inflation regardless of fiscal conditions.
Correlations between policy changes and outcomes directly reveal causal policy effects.
